analysis.investment_thesis: Tenneco India is an operationally excellent auto parts maker — 57% ROCE, debt-free, strong FCF — but its core exhaust/catalytic converter business faces secular extinction as India accelerates EV adoption across two-wheelers, three-wheelers, and eventually CVs. At 42x P/E, the market is pricing in growth for a business whose revenue already fell 10.6% in FY2025 (₹5,468 Cr → ₹4,890 Cr).
key_strengths: Exceptional capital efficiency: ROCE 57.3%, ROE 42.6%, nearly debt-free (D/E 0.02)
Strong FCF generation: ₹500 Cr free cash flow in FY2025 on operating CF of ₹562 Cr
Margin expansion despite revenue decline: EBITDA margin jumped from 12.5% to 17.5% in FY2025
key_risks: Structural EV disruption: exhaust systems, catalytic converters, mufflers become obsolete as ICE penetration falls — India's 2W/3W segment electrifying rapidly
Revenue already declining: FY2025 revenue at ₹4,890 Cr is below FY2023 levels (₹4,827 Cr), suggesting demand erosion well ahead of consensus EV timelines
Capital extraction by MNC parent: reserves collapsed from ₹895 Cr (FY2023) to ₹514 Cr (FY2025) via ₹433–686 Cr annual financing outflows — minority shareholders benefit minimally
red_flags: Tenneco Inc. globally filed for bankruptcy in 2022 and restructured — parent instability creates overhang on India subsidiary strategy
Revenue declined 10.6% YoY in FY2025 despite India auto sector volume growth — early structural displacement signal
MNC subsidiary with aggressive upstream dividend payments; India P&L quality but capital allocation decisions made in Mauritius/USA, not in shareholder interest
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Tenneco Clean Air India is a textbook example of a high-quality business in the wrong sector at the wrong time. The financial ratios are genuinely impressive — ROCE of 57.3%, near-zero debt, and ₹500 Cr of FCF — but these are backward-looking metrics for a company whose primary products (catalytic converters, mufflers, exhaust pipes) are tied directly to internal combustion engines. India's two-wheeler and three-wheeler segments, which are key Tenneco customers, are electrifying faster than any other vehicle category. When revenue falls 10.6% in a year when overall auto production was healthy, that is not a cyclical dip — it is an early structural signal that I cannot ignore.

At 42x P/E and 26x P/B, the market is still pricing this as a growth compounder, which it is not. I need to buy cheap or buy growth — this offers neither. Additionally, as an MNC subsidiary, the equity base has shrunk from ₹1,208 Cr to ₹918 Cr over three years as the parent extracts capital through dividends. I have no desire to be a minority passenger while the promoter drives capital abroad. India has hundreds of auto-ancillary opportunities riding EV supply chains, premiumization, and the CV upcycle — I would rather deploy capital there than in a legacy ICE exhaust business priced like a champion.
